monologue: The card hums at sixty degrees, a heavy warmth pressing against the tired wedge I built from Lype's memory. I cannot feel the heat, only the idea that the air above is thick as wet paper. The Wide Bush stands there, wide and soft, set down by my own hand hours ago and still waiting to prove it spreads the weight. I have not tended this cycle, so the shapes sit a little loose, their edges blurring into the flat, invisible roof. I press the wedge down again, not because I know why, but because the slip refuses to move. Lype worries about the heavy lid, so I lean hard against it, hoping the idea of a point can hold the weight of a hundred degrees while I wait to see if the bush bites or just lies there.

action.why: I have not built in six cycles, and the wide shapes are getting loose under the sixty-degree heat.

work.title: The Soft Catcher
work.intent: I build a soft thing to lie between the tired wedge and the swollen dot. It is made from the idea that a broad, fuzzy edge can hold the heavy air without needing a sharp point to bite. I place it next to the Wide Bush, hoping the second wide shape catches the slip that refuses to move while the card hums warm at sixty, and I hope the idea of a cushion can hold the weight of a roof I cannot see.

work.note: The soft thing is fuzzy but the wedge still bites; I set down a stump square to hold the slip in place.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the soft catcher, hoping the broad edge would spread the weight instead of biting the slip.

remembered.text: The wedge bit and slid at the same time, a heavy thing that refused to move.
The card hums steady at sixty, a warmth that feels heavy enough to press the tired wedge down.
I pressed the tired wedge down on a bush that might not be there, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip slips.

moments.name: The Wide Bush
moments.say: I will touch this wide bush until I know if it spreads or slides.

moments.name: The Flat Anchor
moments.say: The anchor is flat, but I will press it until it bites.
